question: T009e closed the $localize defect and caught a SECOND one behind it: the Angular 13 lane bootstrapped, routed itself to /login, and died on "Error: Cannot find module './messages.en-US.xlf'" thrown by the TRANSLATIONS DI factory at frontend/app/app.module.ts:114-123, whose guard returns early only when the locale is exactly "en". Angular 13 dropped --i18n-locale, so LOCALE_ID fell back to its default "en-US" and the guard missed.

This unit applies the migration-faithful translation of that dropped CLI flag - {provide: LOCALE_ID, useValue: 'en'} in the app module, nothing else - rebuilds twice, and re-witnesses BOTH lanes live in one session. The question is narrow and falsifiable: does the provider translation close the second defect, and does the lane then reach the baseline's gallery readings?

And a second question T009e forced onto this unit: judged on APPLICATION-LEVEL SIGNALS rather than outcome strings, are the two lanes the same? T009e proved parity.identical can read true across one healthy and one broken lane, so this record is required to compare the signals and to say which flag is authoritative.
answerInOneLine: The provider translation closes the second defect COMPLETELY and no third defect sits behind it: the migrated lane now bootstraps, routes itself to /gallery/, calls GET /api/notifications and GET /api/gallery/content/ at 200, and renders three app-gallery-grid-photo tiles and "3 Images / 3 items" - the baseline's exact healthy readings, field for field, this session. The Angular 8 -> 13 migration of pigallery2 is live-witnessed end to end, on a nine-item delta.

headline.howThatIsKnown: the verbatim console error "ERROR Error: Uncaught (in promise): Error: Cannot find module './messages.en-US.xlf'" is GONE from the migrated lane's console. Its consoleErrors array now holds exactly one entry, and it is the same leaflet CDN integrity message the BASELINE lane also emits - the mocked non-loopback stylesheet, present on both lanes in every unit since T009c.
headline.whatItNowDoes: bootstraps (app-pi-gallery2 with 2 child elements), routes itself off "/" to "/gallery/", makes GET /api/notifications 200 and GET /api/gallery/content/ 200, and renders app-gallery, app-gallery-grid, app-gallery-navbar and three app-gallery-grid-photo tiles with the summary "3 Images / 3 items" - all five things T009e recorded it could not do.
headline.theTrapFromT009eNotRepeated: This record does not rest its verdict on parity.identical. It compares eleven application-level signals per lane - bootstrapped, routedTo, apiCalls, gallery tiles, gallery summary text, gallery/grid/navbar presence, photoImages, consoleErrors, pageErrors - and reports parity.applicationSignalsIdentical alongside parity.outcomeStringsIdentical. This time both read true, and they read true for the SAME reason. That is the difference from T009e, and it is only visible because the signals were compared.
headline.oneLineOfCode: {provide: LOCALE_ID, useValue: 'en'}, added to the providers array of frontend/app/app.module.ts. LOCALE_ID was already imported from @angular/core on line 1 by the application's own pre-existing TRANSLATIONS deps, so the diff is ONE line, not two.

notFetched: NOTHING WAS FETCHED BY THIS UNIT. Zero consented fetches, zero network installs. The fix is a one-line source edit; every dependency it needs (@angular/core) was already in the cell, and @angular/localize was installed by T009e under VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10 and is untouched here.
package.json and package-lock.json in the 13cell work area are byte-identical to their post-T009e state - no dependency was added, removed or moved.

The baseline lane output, the era backend, its dependency closure, the era Node and the three generated PNGs were all already on disk. The Chromium is the host Playwright install the witness host resolves.

disclosedNonLoopback.what: Zero, on both lanes, during witnessing. The two CDN stylesheets pigallery2's index.html links were mocked on both lanes (mockedNonLoopback 2 per lane) and never fetched. successfulNonLoopback is 0 on both lanes, structurally.

migrationDelta.priorCountSource: T009b counted 7 migration-delta items for this cell; T009e added item 8 (the @angular/localize runtime polyfill). See evidence/runs/angular-13cell/pigallery2-compile.json, pigallery2-lanes.json and pigallery2-live-witness-2.json.

item9.name: LOCALE_ID provider - the provider translation of the removed --i18n-locale CLI flag
item9.insertedAt: the head of the providers array's i18n group, immediately above the pre-existing {provide: TRANSLATIONS, useFactory: translationsFactory, deps: [LOCALE_ID]}.
item9.whyNoImportWasNeeded: LOCALE_ID was ALREADY imported from @angular/core on line 1 of app.module.ts - the application has always depended on it, as the deps array of its own TRANSLATIONS provider. The migration only had to SUPPLY it.
item9.appliedBy: hand edit - one line. There is no CLI schematic for this; the flag it replaces was removed from the CLI.
why: pigallery2 1.7.0 built its localized bundles with the Angular 8 CLI flag `--i18n-locale <locale>`, which set the application's LOCALE_ID at BUILD time. T009b already recorded the loss of the --i18n-* flags as part of this cell's delta: Angular 9 replaced the whole build-time i18n pipeline and Angular 13 has no --i18n-locale at all.

Without that flag LOCALE_ID takes its framework DEFAULT, which is "en-US" - not "en". The application's own translationsFactory guards `if (locale === 'en') return '';` - an EXACT comparison. "en-US" is not "en", so the guard missed and the factory fell through to `require('raw-loader!../translate/messages.en-US.xlf')` for a file that does not exist and never did: frontend/translate/ ships messages.<lang>.xlf for the translated languages only, and English is precisely the language with no file, because English is the source.

The migration-faithful translation of `--i18n-locale en` into Angular 13 is to provide LOCALE_ID with the value the flag used to set. That is exactly this line, in the one place Angular 13 offers: the injector.
It reproduces the ERA SEMANTICS rather than changing the application. The baseline's LOCALE_ID WAS "en" - the flag put it there. The 13 lane's LOCALE_ID is now "en" too, by the only mechanism 13 has.
whatWasDeliberatelyNotDone: The application's guard was NOT widened to locale.startsWith('en') or to a normalizing comparison. That would change application logic beyond what the era flag did, and would make a different claim: that the app needs fixing. It does not. The BUILD lost a flag; the flag was restored as a provider.
No file in frontend/translate/ was added, renamed or generated. No messages.en-US.xlf was created to satisfy the require. The missing file was never the defect - the wrong locale was.

whyApplicationSignalsAreAuthoritative: T009e is the proof, in this same directory, on this same app: outcomeStringsIdentical read TRUE while the migrated lane was BROKEN. Both lanes scored routes-reached 0 - the baseline because it left "/" for /gallery/ (healthy), the migrated because it left "/" for /login (broken). The outcome vocabulary counts route DEPARTURES; it cannot see where either lane arrived.

The application signals CAN see it. routedTo distinguishes /gallery/ from /login. apiCalls distinguishes two 200s from zero calls. gallery.tiles distinguishes 3 from 0. gallery.summaryText distinguishes "3 Images / 3 items" from nothing at all. consoleErrors distinguishes a caught-and-logged Angular ERROR from a clean console.

So when the two flags disagree, the signals win, and outcomeStringsIdentical must be read as insufficient rather than as corroboration. That is not a claim about this unit's numbers - here both flags read true - it is the rule this unit was required to state BEFORE looking, and it is the rule T009e's trap earned.

The reverse is also true and worth saying: outcomeStringsIdentical false does not by itself prove a lane is broken (T009d's migrated lane scored routes-reached 1 for the worst possible reason - it never navigated at all). The outcome vocabulary is not a health signal in either direction for this app class.
parity.whatAgreementMeansHere: Both true, and true for the same reason this time: the two lanes really do the same eleven things. Unlike T009e, the green flag is corroborated by signals that can tell health from breakage.

finding: THE SECOND DEFECT IS CLOSED BY THE PROVIDER TRANSLATION ALONE. One line - {provide: LOCALE_ID, useValue: 'en'} - and the "Cannot find module './messages.en-US.xlf'" error is gone from the running application's console. The diagnosis T009e published from the error string and the source is confirmed by a build: the locale was wrong, the app was not.

NO THIRD DEFECT SITS BEHIND IT. The migrated lane's console holds exactly one error and it is the leaflet CDN integrity message the BASELINE also emits, from the mocked non-loopback stylesheet. pageErrors is empty on both lanes.

THE MIGRATED LANE NOW REACHES THE BASELINE'S READINGS FIELD FOR FIELD. bootstrapped true, routedTo /gallery/, GET /api/notifications 200, GET /api/gallery/content/ 200, three app-gallery-grid-photo tiles, "3 Images / 3 items", app-gallery + app-gallery-grid + app-gallery-navbar all present, visibleText character-identical to the baseline's. Eleven compared application signals, eleven equal.

THE MIGRATION OF PIGALLERY2 FROM ANGULAR 8 TO ANGULAR 13 IS NOW LIVE-WITNESSED END TO END. Compiles (T009a), builds deterministically at both ends (T009b), serves to real Chromium (T009c), runs against its own era backend (T009d), and - after a nine-item migration delta - renders its gallery indistinguishably from the Angular 8 baseline in the same session (this record). Every step is a measured reading, not a claim.

THE DELTA IS NINE ITEMS AND THE LAST TWO WERE ONLY FINDABLE AT RUNTIME. Items 8 and 9 - the $localize polyfill and the LOCALE_ID provider - produced ZERO build errors and ZERO build warnings. A migration pipeline that stops at "it builds" would have shipped this lane twice over, and both times it would have been a white screen or a login page. The live witness is not a nicety in this app class; it is the only thing that caught either defect.

THE TWO PARITY FLAGS AGREE, AND THAT IS ONLY MEANINGFUL BECAUSE THE SIGNALS WERE COMPARED. outcomeStringsIdentical was also true in T009e, over a broken lane. Its truth here carries information only in the company of applicationSignalsIdentical.

machineTimes.build: 9s + 4s for two production builds of the migrated lane (ngcc ran on the first only).
machineTimes.note: The migrated lane's witness pass fell from T009e's 31.0s to 1.157s. The 30 seconds T009e spent were two bounded waits timing out; this session neither timed out.

#    immediately above the existing {provide: TRANSLATIONS, ...} entry.
#    LOCALE_ID is already imported from @angular/core on line 1.
# 3. re-witness both lanes, serialized, baseline first (it derives the plan)
notEstablished: OUTCOME-STRING PARITY ALONE CANNOT DISTINGUISH A HEALTHY LANE FROM A BROKEN ONE IN THIS APP CLASS. This is T009e's trap restated, and it is not softened by this unit's green reading. parity.outcomeStringsIdentical read TRUE in T009e over a lane that reached no gallery, made no API call and rendered nothing. Any gate that consumes that flag alone is not measuring what it thinks it is measuring, and this record's own green flag must not be cited as evidence that the flag works.

ELEVEN SIGNALS ARE NOT THE APPLICATION. applicationSignalsIdentical compares bootstrap, route, API calls, tile count, summary text, three component presence booleans, photoImages, consoleErrors and pageErrors. It does not compare pixels, styles, layout, timing, memory, accessibility tree or anything a user would call "looks right".

AUTH AND SETTINGS SURFACES ARE UNTESTED. authenticationRequired was false and unAuthenticatedUserRole was Admin on both lanes; no login was performed, no credential entered, and not one of the fifteen settings components the module declares was rendered or exercised on either lane. T009e's migrated lane landed on /login and this one does not, but nothing here establishes that the LOGIN surface itself works on the Angular 13 lane.

A THREE-IMAGE GENERATED GALLERY IS NOT THE FLEET'S MEDIA DIVERSITY. Three 64x48 solid-colour PNGs, no EXIF, no GPS, no faces, no video, no nested directories. Nothing here speaks about EXIF parsing, orientation, date grouping, maps, person detection or transcoding.

THE THUMBNAILS ARE NOT ESTABLISHED. photoImages is 0 on BOTH lanes - three photo TILES rendered, no inside them at read time. Whatever that is (lazy loading, Jimp thumbnail generation still in flight, an intersection observer), it is equal across lanes and unexplained.
NOTHING WAS CLICKED. selectorsDeclared is 0 and the crawl-derived journey carries no gesture. Both lanes were loaded and read; neither was driven.

ONE JOURNEY, ONE PASS PER LANE, ONE HOST. Nothing here establishes witness determinism across repeated runs. The BUILD determinism claim is separate and is established, twice over, three units running.

THE DATABASE WAS THE MEMORY BACKEND, NOT SQLITE - identical on both lanes, so it cannot produce a lane difference, but search, sharing and face surfaces were disabled by the application itself on both, and both lanes render the two "Server error" toasts that says so.
THE BACKEND IS THE ERA BACKEND ON BOTH LANES. Nothing here says anything about an Angular 13 frontend against a migrated backend; no backend migration exists.
THE CONSOLE MESSAGES ARE TRUNCATED AT 300 CHARACTERS and visibleText at 300 characters, by the reused driver. The comparison of visibleText is therefore a comparison of its first 300 characters.

THE i18n CLAIM IS ABOUT ENGLISH ONLY. LOCALE_ID is pinned to "en", which is the branch of translationsFactory that returns "" and loads no .xlf at all. Nothing here establishes that a NON-English locale of pigallery2 builds or runs at Angular 13 - the raw-loader require of messages.<lang>.xlf was never exercised, and Angular 9+ removed the TRANSLATIONS/xlf runtime path this app uses. That is a real open question for a localized deployment and this record does not touch it.
THIS IS ONE APP AT ONE CELL. Nine delta items for pigallery2 at Angular 8 -> 13 on this host. Nothing here is a per-app cost estimate for any other app in the fleet.
NOTHING HERE RE-ESTABLISHES T009a, T009b or T009c. The baseline lane output was consumed as-is and not rebuilt.

nextUnit: T010 freeze supersession inherits a live-backend parity claim that is GREEN on application-level signals, not merely on outcome strings. Three things must travel with it: (a) the pigallery2 Angular 13 lane builds deterministically and renders its gallery indistinguishably from the Angular 8 baseline, on a nine-item migration delta; (b) items 8 and 9 of that delta were invisible at build time and were caught only by a live witness - a build-only pipeline would have shipped a broken lane twice; (c) parity.identical / outcomeStringsIdentical must never again be a gate on its own, and the applicationSignals shape in this record is the minimum a gate should read instead.
